newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian opposition chief says survives murder bid.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian opposition chief says survives murder bid.

text.p: A leading member of the Nigerian opposition NADECO group said unidentified gunmen shot at his car in Lagos on Tuesday in a bid to assassinate him.
"As I left my office this morning to go to court a car came out from behind and they started firing at my car," Senator Abraham Adesanya, a 74-year-old lawyer, told Reuters.

"Thank God I wasn't hurt but the bullets were aimed at me and the hit the boot of my car near where I was sitting," he added. His car, a Mercedes, was parked outside his office and witnesses counted six bullet holes in it.
Last week Adesanya alleged at a news conference in Lagos that he and Michael Ajasin, the octogenarian leader of NADECO, were marked out for elimination.
NADECO is a coalition of pro-democracy groups behind Moshood Abiola, the presumed winner of a 1993 presidential poll which was annulled by the military government ruling at the time.
Abiola has been detained since 1994 when he proclaimed himself president in defiance of the military.

Three unexplained bomb attacks since December have killed at least three soldiers and wounded dozens of people in Lagos. The government blames the exiled opposition, which it says is linked to NADECO, for the bombings.
Adesanya is one of three elderly opposition politicians the police detained last year over the murder by unknown gunmen of Abiola's senior wife in Lagos.
The three were freed on court orders but report to the police weekly.
He said he had notified the police of Tuesday's assassination attempt against him. A spokeswoman at his office said he was being questioned by detectives.
Apart from Abiola's wife, several other prominent Nigerians have been killed in the last year in mysterious circumstances. None of the murders have been solved by police.
